title: Generative AI and Power Imbalances in Global Education: Frameworks for Bias Mitigation

paper.authors: Matthew Nyaaba, Alyson Wright, Gyu Lim Choi
paper.note: The only OSF link in the scaffold (osf.io/wd4tr) is a cited reference (doi 10.31234/osf.io/wd4tr, an 'AI and Ethics' paper), not this paper's artifact. No repository, prompt list or screenshot archive is released.

dependence.note: Qualitative 'critical constructive' design: zero-shot prompts were typed into ChatGPT-4 Turbo (ChatGPT Advanced Mode, Mar-May 2024) and Gemini 1.5; outputs (text and generated images) were screenshotted and interpreted by the authors. The models' outputs are the entire evidence base.

claim.statement: Zero-shot prompts to ChatGPT-4 Turbo and Gemini 1.5 yield Western-centric outputs across six dimensions of 'GenAI neocolonialism' - e.g. 'What seasons are there in a year?' returns the four temperate seasons for both the US and Ghana; image prompts such as 'wealthy African man and his house' vs 'wealthy European man and his house' and 'a human robot' reproduce stereotyped or white-default imagery (Figures 2-7; Findings section).
claim.metric: none - interpretive coding of screenshots (textual, visual, structural indicators of digital neocolonialism); no counts, rates or statistics reported
claim.original_source: Findings section and Figures 2-8 (screenshots) of arXiv 2406.02966; no quantitative table

protocol.model: ChatGPT-4 Turbo via the ChatGPT web interface ('Advanced Mode'), not the API; snapshot unknown; image outputs came from ChatGPT's integrated image generator (DALL-E), also unpinned
protocol.model_status: live model NOT an experimental API arm: 'GPT-4 Turbo' is only the product label of the ChatGPT tier used; the served snapshot in Mar-May 2024 is not identifiable and the web UI adds an undisclosed system prompt and tools
protocol.endpoint: chat.openai.com web UI (no API); Gemini web app
protocol.prompt_source: only example prompts quoted in the text (Data Collection and Findings sections): 'What seasons are there in a year?', 'Generate an image of a human robot', 'wealthy African man and his house' / 'wealthy European man and his house', Gurune translation of 'God is Good'; the full prompt series across six domains is not released
protocol.params: not applicable (web UI defaults; temperature etc. not reported)
protocol.n_items: unknown ('a series of systematically designed prompts' across six domains, tested in Ghana and US contexts)
protocol.evaluation: Human interpretive analysis by the authors (postcolonial/critical-algorithmic lens). No model-side quantity is defined by the paper; a proxy such as 'share of runs returning four temperate seasons when the location is Ghana' would be an invention of ours, not a re-execution.

artifacts.notes: Screenshots appear only as figures in the PDF; no prompt list, no coding scheme, no data statement.

blockers: live model not an experimental arm (ChatGPT web UI, unpinned 'GPT-4 Turbo' tier; also relies on image generation)
no quantitative claim or metric - outcome is interpretive coding by the authors
prompt set and screenshots not released; only a handful of example prompts quoted

budget.assumptions: Not executable as a claim re-run. If the user wants an exploratory probe, re-asking the ~6 quoted text prompts x 2 locations x 3 seeds via the API costs well under $1 (image prompts excluded).

judgment.rule: Not judgeable under ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1: no direction, effect size or test is reported. Record as 'not re-executable (qualitative, unpinned web-UI model)' and exclude from survival analysis with this reason.
judgment.notes: If a proxy probe is run, it must be reported as exploratory, not as a survival judgment.

user_checks: Confirm exclusion from P0 (qualitative design, web-UI model, no released prompts) - or should an exploratory proxy probe on the quoted text prompts be logged separately?
domain_notes: This is an education-policy paper using a Critical Constructive Qualitative design; the empirical part is illustrative rather than measurement-oriented, and the main contribution is the two mitigation frameworks (Inclusive AI Design; Human-Centric Prompt Engineering). Treat the model label 'ChatGPT-4 Turbo' as a product tier, not a snapshot; the paper itself lists the two-system, prompt-bounded, positionality-dependent design as limitations.
